project.name: codeintel
project.description:
Code Intelligence client - native, in-process ToolCallbacks that let an agent search a tenant's indexed codebase, walk its deterministic code graph (callers / impact), and get grounded, cited code answers. Thin HTTP client over the standalone `code-intel` microservice (see the repo's top-level `code-intel/` folder + docs/SDLC-CODEBASE-RAG-DESIGN.md); this module is only the core-side bridge, exactly parallel to how `knowledge`'s KnowledgeSearchToolCallback wraps the sidecar.
Trust model: server-to-server. core has already authenticated the user and holds TenantContext; this client forwards TenantContext.tenantId as X-Tenant-Id plus a shared secret X-Internal-Token to the code-intel service running with auth_mode=internal - the same posture core already uses toward the Python sidecar. No per-tenant BYOK credential is needed (the service is operator-run infrastructure, not a third-party API a tenant brings their own key for), so unlike sarvam/e2b there is no credential module dependency.
Enablement: gated by `code-intel.enabled` (default false). When off, the CodeIntelClient bean is absent and AgentToolProvider's ObjectProvider lookup returns empty - zero behavior change until an operator points this at a running service. The five read-only retrieval/graph tools (search_code, code_callers, code_callees, code_impact, code_graph_stats) are auto-offered to every agent via AgentToolProvider#resolveCodeIntelTools - zero execution risk. The five write/execute workspace tools (create_code_workspace, apply_code_changes, run_in_code_workspace, diff_code_workspace, delete_code_workspace) are NOT auto-offered anywhere yet (see AgentToolProvider#resolveCodeWorkspaceTools's javadoc for the deliberately-unwired state and what's missing to safely turn it on); the two consequential ones (apply/run) also always route through core/approval's HumanApprovalGateService + a registered ApprovalActionExecutor before code-intel's own apply/run endpoint is ever called, regardless of what code-intel's own internal guardrail policy would independently allow - see ApplyCodeChangesToolCallback / RunInCodeWorkspaceToolCallback.
Depends on: security (TenantContext), approval (HumanApprovalGateService + ApprovalActionExecutor, for the workspace write/execute gate only), plus spring-web (RestClient) and the Spring AI tool API (ToolCallback) - the same tool type `knowledge` implements.
